consensus_summary: Primary consensus: the north/north country is the quarter from which divine judgment and invading armies (esp. Assyria/Babylon) come against Israel/Judah, reflecting invasion routes; it also denotes the land of exile/return. Widely noted secondary motifs: God's mountain/Zaphon and eschatological northern foes; satanic/evil readings are minority.
book_summary: The north is the hidden quarter and the direction from which concealed invaders emerge; the north country gathers the nations that spoil Babylon; the enemy seeks his seat in its hidden recesses; it is also the direction of God's mountain.
consensus_core_identification: Direction/source of hostile invasion and divine judgment (prototypically Mesopotamian powers against Israel/Judah), plus exile/return; secondarily God's mountain.
book_core_identification: Hidden quarter; direction of concealed invaders; gathering-place of nations that spoil Babylon; place where the enemy seeks his seat; also God's mountain.
boundary_disagreement: Book makes 'hidden/concealed,' the spoiling of Babylon, and the enemy seeking a seat definitional; consensus keeps judgment-on-Israel via northern empires as the primary case-set and treats Zaphon and Isa 14 enemy-ambition strands as separate secondary motifs.
material_contradiction: None. The book does not deny northern invasion/judgment; it reweights and recombines overlapping motifs.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on invaders-from-the-north and God's mountain, so the central category is not replaced. The book preserves those referents but materially changes extension and precision by centering 'hidden quarter,' nations spoiling Babylon (Jer 50–51; Rev 17), and the enemy seeking a seat (Isa 14), which consensus lists mainly as secondary or alternative. That is boundary/extension disagreement without core contradiction → REFINED.
strongest_objection: Dominant prophetic usage (esp. Jeremiah 1–6 etc.) makes the north primarily the source of judgment on Judah through Babylon, not a definitional 'hidden' seat of the enemy or primarily the coalition that spoils Babylon; the book may over-integrate secondary strands into the core gloss.
